explain.say: Car engines make some harmful gases: poisonous carbon monoxide, unburnt fuel, and nitrogen oxides that cause smog. A catalytic converter in the exhaust changes most of them into less harmful gases.

explain.say: The metals platinum, palladium and rhodium are catalysts: they help reactions happen without being used up. Carbon monoxide and unburnt fuel react with oxygen to make carbon dioxide and water, and nitrogen oxides are split into nitrogen and oxygen.

faq.q: What harmful gases come out of a car engine?
faq.a: Engines make carbon monoxide, which is poisonous, unburnt fuel called hydrocarbons, and nitrogen oxides, which cause smog and harm lungs. Diesels also make soot.

faq.q: Why is the inside a honeycomb?
faq.a: The honeycomb has thousands of thin channels, so the gas flows easily while touching a huge area of catalyst-coated wall. More surface means faster cleaning.
asks: What is inside a catalytic converter?

faq.a: A catalyst is a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up itself. In a car, platinum, palladium and rhodium do this.
asks: Why are there precious metals in a catalytic converter?

faq.q: What reactions happen in a catalytic converter?
faq.a: Carbon monoxide gains oxygen to become carbon dioxide, unburnt fuel burns to carbon dioxide and water, and nitrogen oxides are broken into harmless nitrogen and oxygen.
asks: What does a catalytic converter turn gases into?

faq.q: Does a catalytic converter stop carbon dioxide?
faq.a: No. It turns harmful gases into carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water. Carbon dioxide comes from burning any carbon fuel, so only using less fuel or going electric cuts it.
asks: Is a catalytic converter good for climate change?

facts: A three-way catalytic converter tackles carbon monoxide, unburnt hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides at the same time.
Catalytic converters work best once they reach a few hundred degrees Celsius.
They contain small amounts of platinum, palladium and rhodium, which is why thieves sometimes steal them.
